We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions to synthesize target SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1.

We have already applied template 647549 (amide formation? Actually it broke amide to give O-CO-aryl and aniline). The apply_template gave precursors: ('COc1cccc(N)c1', 'Nc1c(C(=O)O)nnn1Cc1ccc(CN2CC(F)C2)cc1'). So step1 retrosynthesis: target -> two fragments: an anisole aniline (COc1cccc(N)c1) and a heterocycle with carboxylic acid (Nc1c(C(=O)O)nnn1Cc1ccc(CN2CC(F)C2)cc1). Good.

Now we need further steps to break these into simpler precursors, total 3 reactions (so 2 more steps). For each fragment we need to propose retrosynthetic steps.

First fragment: COc1cccc(N)c1 is anisidine (para? Actually methoxy at position 1, amine at position 4). Could be made via SN2? Actually we need to form C-N bond from halide to amine (SN2). The guidance mentions SN2 reaction where halide is leaving group. So we can propose to get anisidine from 4-chloro- anisole (COc1ccc(Cl)cc1) + ammonia (NH3). That is SN2 (aryl halide? Actually SNAr maybe). But they said SN2 with halide functional group broken. So we can use template that breaks aryl halide to give amine. We have template 1914393 (from earlier search) which seems to be aryl halide to amine (Cl-CH2-aryl + amine). Actually the template 1914393 retro smarts: [#7:7]-[C:6]-[c:5]1...>>Cl-[CH2...]. That is for benzylic halide? Not aryl. But we have a template for aryl halide to amine maybe 647476? That one breaks aryl halide to amine? Let's check 647476 retro: [O;D1;H0:6]=[C;H0;D3;+0:5](-[c:7])-[NH;D2;+0:4]-[c:3]:[cH;D2;+0:1]:[c:2]>>Cl-[c;H0;D3;+0:1](:[c:2]):[c:3]-[NH2;D1;+0:4]. That's aryl halide to amine? It converts aryl amide to aryl chloride? Not sure.

But we can search for template that breaks aryl halide to amine. Use search with functional_groups_broken ["aryl halide"] and functional_groups_formed ["primary amines"] we already did and got some templates. The first result 383325 is a transformation from aryl bromide to amine with nitro? Not ideal. But we can use any template that matches our anisidine.

We need to check if template 383325 matches COc1cccc(N)c1. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching.
